plants.name: Adiantum raddianum
plants.tip: One dry day costs you the fronds. Keep the compost damp, and cut a crisped plant to the base to force fresh growth.
plants.colour: Fresh mid-green fans on wiry black stems

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Fragrans'
plants.tip: The florist's maidenhair, sold in tight pots that dry out fast. Water before the surface goes pale, not after.
plants.colour: Dense pale green fans, finely divided

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Fritz Luthi'
plants.tip: Compact enough for a terrarium or a bathroom shelf. Dry air browns the outer fronds first.
plants.colour: Compact mid-green fans held in overlapping tiers

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Kensington Gem'
plants.tip: More robust than most delta maidenhairs, but still unforgiving of a dry rootball. Water from below to spare the crown.
plants.colour: Broad deep green fans on dark, arching stems

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Microphyllum'
plants.tip: The small leaflets crisp faster than larger forms. Stand the pot on damp gravel rather than misting it.
plants.colour: Very small mid-green pinnae, lacy overall

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Gracillimum'
plants.tip: The finest fronds of the group and the least forgiving. It wants steady damp and no draught from a door or vent.
plants.colour: Extremely fine, feathery light green foliage

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Elegans'
plants.tip: Grows lax and looks best raised on a stand. Trim spent fronds at the base to stop the middle going bare.
plants.colour: Soft green fans on lax, trailing stems

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Variegatum'
plants.tip: The white flecking fades in a dim corner and scorches in sun. Bright indirect light holds the pattern.
plants.colour: Mid-green pinnae flecked and streaked with white

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Ocean Spray'
plants.tip: Sold as a dense dome that hides a dry centre. Check the compost in the middle of the pot, not at the rim.
plants.colour: Pale sea-green fans with a slightly ruffled edge

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Pacific Maid'
plants.tip: Vigorous for a maidenhair and quick to fill a pot. Repot once it starts drying out within a day or two.
plants.colour: Broad, overlapping bright green pinnae

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Pacotti'
plants.tip: Holds a tight shape, so a bare patch means the roots dried out. Cut it back hard and keep it damp.
plants.colour: Dense dark green fronds on a compact, upright plant

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Brilliantelse'
plants.tip: A nursery selection grown for speed, and it drinks accordingly. In summer it may want water every other day.
plants.colour: Glossy fresh green fans, densely packed

plants.name: Adiantum raddianum 'Tinctum'
plants.tip: The pink sits only on new growth, so feed lightly through summer to keep fresh fronds coming.
plants.colour: New fronds flushed pink, ageing to mid-green

plants.name: Adiantum tenerum
plants.tip: Coarser than delta maidenhair and just as intolerant of drying. The stems snap, so lift it by the pot.
plants.colour: Large fan-shaped pinnae in bright green on black stems

plants.name: Adiantum tenerum 'Farleyense'
plants.tip: Sterile, so it can only be divided, never grown from spores. It sulks below about 15C and wants steady damp.
plants.colour: Large, ruffled, overlapping pale green pinnae

plants.name: Adiantum tenerum 'Scutum Roseum'
plants.tip: The rose flush lasts a week or two on each new frond, so warmth through summer is what keeps the colour going.
plants.colour: New fronds a strong rose pink, maturing mid-green

plants.name: Adiantum tenerum 'Lady Moxam'
plants.tip: Dense growth traps moisture, so give it moving air as well as humidity or the crown rots.
plants.colour: Densely overlapping, slightly ruffled bright green pinnae

plants.name: Adiantum hispidulum
plants.tip: Tougher than the delta maidenhairs and forgives a brief dry spell, though the frond tips still crisp.
plants.colour: Bronze-pink new fronds hardening to rough, dull green

plants.name: Adiantum hispidulum 'Bronze Venus'
plants.tip: Bright indirect light brings the bronze out. In shade the new fronds come through plain green instead.
plants.colour: New fronds deep copper-bronze, ageing to mid-green

plants.name: Adiantum capillus-veneris
plants.tip: It grows on wet limestone in the wild, so hard tap water suits it. Drying out is the thing that kills it.
plants.colour: Delicate pale green wedges on hair-fine black stems

plants.name: Adiantum peruvianum
plants.tip: Coin-sized pinnae that snap easily, so keep it where nothing brushes past. Warmth and damp air all year.
plants.colour: Very large, coin-sized pinnae, pink when new

plants.name: Adiantum trapeziforme
plants.tip: Fronds reach about a metre, so it needs floor space rather than a shelf. Stake the arching stems if they splay.
plants.colour: Large diamond-shaped pinnae on arching fronds

plants.name: Adiantum macrophyllum
plants.tip: Fewer, bigger leaflets than most maidenhairs. Deep shade and constant damp suit it, as does a closed case.
plants.colour: Few large pinnae, coppery pink when new, then deep green

plants.name: Adiantum formosum
plants.tip: Spreads by underground rhizome and surfaces away from the parent, so give it a wide pot or a bed of its own.
plants.colour: Tall triangular fronds, dark green on black stems

plants.name: Adiantum caudatum
plants.tip: Frond tips root where they touch soil, so peg one into a second pot to make a new plant.
plants.colour: Narrow arching fronds, hairy, mid-green

plants.name: Adiantum reniforme
plants.tip: Not fern-shaped at all: each frond is a single kidney-shaped blade. It rots in soggy compost, so ease off in winter.
plants.colour: Single round kidney-shaped blades on fine black stalks

plants.name: Adiantum polyphyllum
plants.tip: Big and vigorous for a maidenhair. A deep pot keeps the roots cool and slows the drying that kills it.
plants.colour: Large arching fronds with many small blue-green pinnae

plants.name: Adiantum concinnum
plants.tip: Naturally drooping, so it suits a hanging pot. The thin fronds crisp quickly above a radiator.
plants.colour: Drooping, finely divided fronds in soft light green

plants.name: Adiantum diaphanum
plants.tip: Small enough for a terrarium, where the closed air suits its thin fronds. It cannot cope with a dry room.
plants.colour: Small dark green pinnae, thin and almost translucent

plants.name: Adiantum flabellulatum
plants.tip: Stiffer and more leathery than most maidenhairs, so slower to crisp. It still wants soil that stays damp.
plants.colour: Stiff fan-shaped fronds, leathery dark green

plants.name: Adiantum latifolium
plants.tip: Runs from the rhizome and will colonise a bed, so keep it potted unless you actually want the spread.
plants.colour: Broad, widely spaced pale green pinnae

plants.name: Adiantum seemannii
plants.tip: Grown for the blue-grey cast, which is strongest on new fronds. Warmth and humidity keep them coming.
plants.colour: Drooping fronds with blue-grey, wedge-shaped pinnae

plants.name: Adiantum philippense
plants.tip: Arching fronds that root at the tip. Pot the tip on rather than trying to split the crown, which resents it.
plants.colour: Arching fronds with half-moon pinnae

plants.name: Adiantum pedatum
plants.tip: Hardy and deciduous, so it dies back in autumn. Clear the old fronds in late winter before the new crooks rise.
plants.colour: Blue-green pinnae in a horseshoe on glossy black stems

plants.name: Adiantum aleuticum
plants.tip: Wants shade and a moist, leafy soil. A spell of full sun bleaches the fronds within a fortnight.
plants.colour: Fan of blue-green fingers on near-black wiry stems

plants.name: Adiantum aleuticum 'Imbricatum'
plants.tip: Low and slow, so it is easily swamped by neighbours. Keep the ground around it clear.
plants.colour: Overlapping blue-grey pinnae on a low, tight plant

plants.name: Adiantum aleuticum 'Subpumilum'
plants.tip: Stays under about 15cm, which suits a trough or a shady rockery. The soil must never bake dry.
plants.colour: Dwarf blue-green fans, rarely above 15cm

plants.name: Adiantum venustum
plants.tip: Spreads slowly by rhizome into a carpet. Old fronds hold through winter, so shear them off in early spring.
plants.colour: Triangular fronds, bronze in spring, turning mid-green

plants.name: Adiantum x mairisii
plants.tip: A hybrid that takes more cold than the tender maidenhairs, but it still wants shelter from wind and winter wet.
plants.colour: Arching mid-green fronds on dark, thin stems

plants.name: Adiantum aethiopicum
plants.tip: Dies back in drought and returns from the rhizome, so a collapsed plant is often not dead. Keep watering it.
plants.colour: Light green fans on fine black stems, loosely held
